label: conj:schwinger-measure-computational-time
title: Computational-time identification: the binding Borel variable is the loop proper time
html:
Conjecture (computational-time identification of the Schwinger variable).

Let s denote the Schwinger proper-time variable of the \zeta-regularized one-loop photon determinant on the Bring Jacobian, whose loop expansion weighs proper time by the scale-invariant measure \varsigma\,\frac{ds}{s} with unit \varsigma (def:schwinger-measure-unit; the shape is the unique scale-invariant density, the unit is what remains open). Let N(n) denote the binding normalizer forced by the normalization bridge — the unique strip N(n) = (n-1)! making the binding generating function the carrier of the proved depth-2 confluent kernel (the normalization leg of conj:qdifference-kernel-prolongation-symbol).

The framework premises are named:

  • P1 (scale-freedom): the substrate is scale-free; the locally realized modulus q_0 is local data, not a structural scale of the substrate.
  • P2 (computational time): proper time is computational time — s counts the substrate's computation steps.

Statement. The binding sector's Borel variable and the loop's Schwinger proper time s are the same substrate object. Under P2 both are the substrate's computational time, and the identification takes the quantitative form: the normalizer is the n-th moment of the loop's proper-time measure,

N(n) \;=\; \int_0^\infty s^{\,n}\, e^{-s}\,\varsigma\,\frac{ds}{s} \;=\; \varsigma\,(n-1)! .

Conditional consequences. Both are conditional on this conjecture (together with P1/P2 where noted); neither is a derivation of it.

  1. The unit is forced: \varsigma = 1. The Lean-proved identity n \cdot N(n) = n! rescales under a unit \varsigma to \varsigma \cdot n! = n!, so \varsigma = 1 exactly; the rival value \varsigma = \tfrac12 gives n!/2 \neq n! (an exact distinguisher, proved unconditionally in the sibling Lean). Conditionally, this fixes the unit — one nat per proper-time e-fold, with k_B = 1 so that entropy is counted in nats (prop:boltzmann-constant).
  2. The \tfrac12 is located per-channel bar-even. With total unit \varsigma = 1, the working per-channel coefficient \tfrac12\,a_0 = 1/(8\pi) — where a_0 = 1/(4\pi) is the derived two-dimensional heat-kernel unit entering the \alpha_{EM} insertion (prop:em-coupling-fixed-point) — arises from the doubled-pair channel split. For the doubled bar pair (q, q^{-1}) \leftrightarrow (t, 1/t) and a bar-even integrand f, i.e. f(t) = f(1/t) under the bar involution t \mapsto 1/t, the exact fold identity \int_0^\infty f(t)\,\tfrac{dt}{t} = 2\int_1^\infty f(t)\,\tfrac{dt}{t} places the \tfrac12 per channel on the bar-even side, while a bar-odd integrand receives 0. This tips the \tfrac12-adjudication toward the \rho-split reading (total unit one, the \tfrac12 in the channel split) and against the energy-Jacobian reading (\varsigma = \tfrac12 on the proper-time side), which would break the moment identity.

The identification is a dictionary premise between two sectors — the \alpha_{EM} loop measure and the binding q-Borel transform. It is stated here as a precise, falsifiable structural claim: a derivation would fix the unit; a refutation would rule the identification out. The two sectors would share one unit, and the binding side's is Lean-forced; the checkable content is the moment identity above, verified exactly at orders n = 1 through 6.

Fibre-level refinement (bar-parity). The statement above is archimedean (q = 1), where the proper time s is real and hence bar-invariant. At the fibre level (q \neq 1) the identification is consistent only in the balanced q-Borel convention: the one-sided normalizer [n-1]_q! is bar-covariant with exact weight q^{-(n-1)(n-2)/2}, so it cannot equal a bar-invariant proper-time object, while the balanced normalizer q^{-(n-1)(n-2)/4}\,[n-1]_q! is exactly bar-invariant with vanishing first-order q-correction. The conjecture is therefore to be read in the balanced convention; the one-sided reading is refuted at q \neq 1 (exact weight mismatch, machine-verified at both substrate pins).

Structure of the open content. The binding generating function enters this paper only formally — the proved normalizer strip, the proved depth-2 recurrence, and formal q-Borel coefficient maps; no binding number is produced by an integral resummation. The conjecture's representability content is therefore a claim about a canonical choice of integral representation for a formally performed operation, and under that reformulation its two levels separate cleanly.

  • Archimedean (q = 1): closed. The proper-time kernel is derived, not chosen: e^{-s}\,ds is the unique positive measure whose \frac{ds}{s}-moments are (n-1)! (Carleman determinacy), and the explicitly constructed family of balanced fibre kernels converges weakly to it — tightness is Lean-proved from the second-moment confluence, so every Prokhorov subsequential limit is the Schwinger measure (conditional only on the classical Prokhorov-selection and moment-passage theorems, carried as instance-free Lean classes).
  • Fibre (q \neq 1): the choice has exact coordinates. The balanced moment functional determines a canonical Jacobi operator J(q) with no convention entering (Favard); the balanced moment problem is indeterminate at q \neq 1, J(q) has deficiency indices (1,1), and its self-adjoint extensions form a circle whose spectral measures are exactly the representing kernels. Three prior descriptions of the ambiguity are one object in three frames: the translate continuum u \in \mathbb{R}_{>0}/\tilde q^{\,\mathbb{Z}} of theta-grid kernels (\tilde q = \sqrt{q}), the nonzero Poisson dual-mode sector of a single log-normal Gaussian — the atomic kernels are its lattice samplings, the absolutely continuous kernel its zero mode — and the self-adjoint-extension circle itself.
  • The closing question, named. What remains open is the distinguished extension. The moment functional is Stieltjes, so the Friedrichs and Krein extensions are canonical candidates requiring no further input. The bar-involution route as first posed is closed in its pushforward reading: the reflection s \mapsto \tilde q^{-1}/s does not act on the extension circle by pushforward at all — the image of an extension measure has bounded support, so its moments grow too slowly to represent the balanced sequence — hence it cannot exchange the extremal extensions in that reading; an action on the Nevanlinna parameter not induced by pushforward remains open. Two structural inputs replace it. First, the family is identified in the classical literature: the balanced kernel family factors exactly as a Stieltjes–Wigert log-normal core — Stieltjes' 1894 indeterminate example at base \sqrt{q} — convolved with a determinate compact Jackson factor, and the one-sided convention is exactly Moak's q-Laguerre family under a pure scaling. Second, as measured: the Friedrichs and Krein atom supports occupy complementary \tilde q-sublattices whose common translate class extrapolates to the unit class u \equiv 1; the bar-fixed classes are Lean-proved to be exactly \{1, \tilde q^{1/2}\}, so the measured alignment lands on one of the two symmetric points. The sharpened open content: derive the extension choice (Friedrichs versus Krein) from substrate structure, or derive the u \equiv 1 alignment that is at present only measured.

The second route reduces to a single analytic statement. For the pure Stieltjes–Wigert core the extremal extensions are explicit: its Jacobi data have the closed form \alpha_k = \tilde q^{\,k-1}(\tilde q^{\,k}(1+\tilde q) - 1), \beta_{k+1} = \tilde q^{\,3k}(\tilde q^{\,k+1} - 1) — Lean-proved at general order (the iterated Jacobi vector in closed form, hence (M^n)_{00} = \tilde q^{\,n(n-1)/2} exactly) — and the Nevanlinna function is the Ramanujan entire function A_{\tilde q^{-1}} up to a constant, so the Krein extension is supported on its zeros and the Friedrichs extension on those zeros shifted by exactly one \tilde q-step; the two occupy complementary sublattices of the integer \tilde q-lattice class.

Transporting that class to the balanced family requires no perturbation argument. Comparing the two families through their moment ratios rather than their Jacobi data makes the transport exact: the factorization gives m_{k+1}/m_k = \tilde q^{\,k} E (1 - p^{\,k+1}) against the core's exact \tilde q^{\,k}, so the class shift is exactly \log_{\tilde q} E with E = q/(q-1), and the whole discrepancy is the single closed-form term \log_{\tilde q}(1 - p^{\,k+1}), which vanishes geometrically. Both ratio identities and the vanishing are Lean-proved. Hence the balanced tropical class is \varphi_1 = \log_{\tilde q} E \bmod 1 — the unit class — by derivation.

What remains is one analytic statement: that the extremal supports are asymptotic to those ratios. It is the same input the pure Stieltjes–Wigert core already requires (the asymptotics of the zeros of A_{\tilde q^{-1}}), so the transport introduces no further analytic debt. Numerically the conclusion holds to 8 \times 10^{-10} at q = 2.0736 and remains consistent, though not certified, on rungs approaching the substrate; at the pins the core certifies but the balanced truncation does not, so no class is claimed there.

  • Selection principles tested (exact outcomes). Singularity matching is uniquely selective in form — a single off-axis output pole datum would pin the kernel exactly — but is data-blind on the data available here: the fibre q-Borel transform is entire, and the only computable output singularity (the positive-axis wall) is exactly translate-invariant; the two reflection-symmetric candidates differ by exactly half a \tilde q-step in the model pole lattice, so a future output datum would discriminate them sharply. Modular-double covariance organizes the family — the family is the dual-frame decomposition of one Gaussian — but does not select: strict self-duality is empty at the substrate, reality of the dual modes re-derives the bar-reflection cut, and the two natural strengthenings (dual-mode positivity; modular inertness) each pin a unique kernel, but different ones.

Nothing downstream depends on this. The conjecture is unchanged in kind; its open fibre content is relocated, with exact coordinates, from the choice of kernel to the choice of self-adjoint extension.
